Action Plan:
1. Patient instructed to have wife call emergency services (ambulance) immediately for possible anaphylaxis after wasp sting with respiratory involvement.  
2. Patient advised to take an oral antihistamine available at home while awaiting ambulance arrival.  
3. Transfer to nearest emergency department via ambulance for further assessment and treatment (e.g., intramuscular epinephrine, monitoring, airway support).  
4. Document penicillin allergy in medical record for future care.  
5. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for consult: Breathing difficulty, chest tightness, lip tingling, and blotchy rash ~15 minutes after wasp sting while gardening.  
• Onset/duration: Symptoms began immediately; ongoing for 15 minutes at time of call.  
• Progression: Shallow breathing and chest tightness persist; no throat swelling reported.  
• Past medical history: Eczema; aerosinusitis.  
• Medications: Antihistamine tablets at home (dose/route/frequency not documented).  
• Allergies: Penicillin (reaction not specified).  
• Social history: Wife present at home; able to call ambulance.

Objective:
• No in-person examination performed (video/telephone consult).  
• Patient-reported findings: lip tingling without visible swelling, chest tightness, shallow breathing, blotchy cutaneous rash.  
• No vital signs available.  
• No imaging or laboratory results available.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute allergic reaction / suspected anaphylaxis:
   - Assessment: Likely anaphylaxis given respiratory symptoms and cutaneous involvement after wasp sting.
   - Differential diagnosis: Local allergic reaction, anxiety/panic, asthma exacerbation.  
   - Investigations planned: To be performed in emergency department (vital signs, airway assessment, possible serum tryptase).  
   - Treatment planned: Immediate EMS activation; patient to take oral antihistamine; expect ED management with intramuscular epinephrine, oxygen, IV fluids, corticosteroids, observation.  
   - Referrals: Emergency medical services now; consider outpatient allergy/immunology referral post-event for venom immunotherapy assessment.

2. Documented drug allergy (penicillin):
   - Assessment: Non-acute; ensure allergy recorded in chart.  
   - Treatment planned: Maintain avoidance; alert future prescribers.  
   - Referrals: None at this time.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: No vital signs, detailed medication list, or detailed allergy reaction description obtained.  
● Internal conflicts: None noted.  
● Transcript quality: Clear audio; occasional minor hesitations but clinically adequate.
